issue: Is a Rule 60(b) motion that adds a new claim, filed while an appeal from the denial of an initial federal habeas petition is still pending, a second or successive habeas petition under 28 U.S.C. § 2244(b)?

sides.position: A Rule 60(b) motion filed while an appeal from the denial of an initial habeas petition is pending is a second or successive habeas petition under § 2244(b), so the district court lacks jurisdiction absent authorization (following Beaty v. Schriro).
cases: Beaty v. Schriro, 554 F.3d 780, 783 n.1 (9th Cir. 2009)

sides.position: A petition filed while an earlier habeas petition is still awaiting adjudication on appeal is not second or successive, because the earlier petition has not been finally adjudicated.
cases: Ching v. United States, 298 F.3d 174, 178 (2d Cir. 2002)
United States v. Santarelli, 929 F.3d 95, 104– 05 (3d Cir. 2019)

this_court: The majority holds that the Rule 60(b) motion is a second or successive petition under Beaty; the concurrence disagrees with Beaty and would adopt the Second and Third Circuit rule.
quote: He wrote separately to register his disagreement with Beaty and to urge the Supreme Court to recognize the circuit split and to adopt the rule stated in Ching v. United States, 298 F.3d 174, 178 (2d Cir. 2002), and United States v. Santarelli, 929 F.3d 95, 104– 05 (3d Cir. 2019).
cite: Alexander Balbuena v. William Sullivan, No. 12-16414 (9th Cir. 2020)
